name: Alicon Castalloy Ltd
title: Alicon Castalloy Ltd - 531147 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Alicon's Q1 FY27 revenue crossed Rs 500 crore with 9.5% EBITDA margin (vs 11.4% last year) as aluminium pass-through lags; management guides 12-15% growth and +1% margin, while capacity is ~90-100% utilised and new Rs 125 crore plant adds ~Rs 500 crore revenue by FY30-31.

summary.headline: Alicon Q1 FY27 crossed Rs 500 crore quarterly sales for first time; total income Rs 579 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA margin 9.5% vs 11.4% last year.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 37% YoY on a consolidated basis, with total income of Rs 579 crore and PAT of Rs 12 crore (+23% YoY). Margins stayed under pressure from aluminium and other input cost inflation, and the European subsidiary declined as legacy programmes ended. Management guided FY27 underlying growth of 12-15% and at least 1% EBITDA margin improvement, and announced a Rs 125 crore leased facility at Shikrapur expected to generate about Rs 500 crore of annual revenue in 4-5 years. Executable order book stands at about Rs 8,450 crore over 2026-2031.

financial_highlights.change: vs 11.4% in last year; management says 11.4% when aluminium impact removed
about 124 tonnes above prior-year Q1 per management; FY26 tonnage 34,000 tonnes

segments.name: Domestic / standalone
segments.commentary: Standalone growth 43.6% reported and 22% underlying; standalone profitability stronger than international. Commercial vehicle business grew about 26% on conversion of recently acquired businesses to mass production.

segments.name: International (Europe, Slovakia plant)
segments.commentary: Softer quarter as mature programmes reached end of life; new programmes including an e-Axle business are in development, with SOP expected from Q3 FY27. Management expects the decline to continue for one or more quarters.

segments.name: Non-automotive
segments.commentary: Only about 2% of the Rs 8,450 crore order book (about Rs 126 crore). Wins include industrial HVAC compressor housings for data centres and first tractor cylinder head business; new dedicated sales team created.

guidance_outlook: FY27 growth guided at 12-15% underlying (excluding aluminium effect), revised up from earlier 10% expectation.
At least 1% EBITDA margin improvement expected in FY27 versus FY26 levels, driven by customer price revisions and internal productivity.
Aluminium pass-through is contractually immediate from 1 April per management; part of manufacturing-cost recovery still under discussion with customers, with closures expected in Q2 and Q3.
Management aspires to margins of 14-15% over time but declined to give a timeline; ROCE of 10.7% in FY26 targeted to reach about 15% through process changes.
Revenue plan of about Rs 1,600 crore by 2030 (Q&A), analyst characterised this as roughly doubling revenue; management confirmed.
Inorganic growth announcement promised by Q4 FY27; further organic capacity investments to be announced.
capex_capacity: Shikrapur leased facility (about 1.36 lakh sq ft, 5 km from existing plant): Rs 125 crore over 2-3 years; possession from 1 September 2026; SOP targeted by March 2027; about Rs 500 crore annual revenue at full run in 4-5 years, with capacity starting at about 3,000 tonnes and rising to about 7,000 tonnes.
Facility will house GDC, LPDC and machining capabilities; funded mainly by internal accruals plus borrowings; about Rs 70 crore of FY27 capex earmarked for it.
Capacity utilisation close to 100% in the last quarter, and above 90% per management.
Plans to free up some capacity over the next two quarters by exiting lower-value 2-wheeler business (market share cut by 1-2%) and reallocate it to higher-value products; handover takes 6-8 months.
Machining share of passenger vehicle tonnage at about 65-70%; management expects this to rise with in-house machining investment.
Management indicated a plan to add roughly 10,000 tonnes of Indian capacity (analyst paraphrase); further investments to be announced.
demand_pricing: Executable order book about Rs 8,450 crore as on 30 June 2026 over 2026-2031, including Q1 wins; excludes ongoing programmes that were already in revenue before FY26. About 40% is export and about 30% of total is deemed export.
Order book mix: EV about 16%, hybrid about 12%, structural (technology-agnostic) about 10%, non-auto about 2%; balance is ICE and 2-wheeler per the call.

Acquisitions in the quarter across auto and non-auto with potential revenue above Rs 450 crore over five years; entry into two large Indian PV and CV OEMs with visibility of about Rs 850 crore over five years.
JLR EV supply running at about 600 sets per week, expected to rise from January 2027 and peak by calendar Q3 2026; management said consumption only marginally reflected in Q1.
Value addition grew about 17.6% in the quarter; management says growth is shifting to higher value-added parts.
Management reports competitive pressure is rising but states Alicon is not fighting on price in differentiated products.

qa_highlights.question: How will the overseas business perform for the rest of FY27 and FY28, and what is the revenue outlook over one to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said European slowdown may persist for one or more quarters but should reverse from Q4 FY27 with new e-Axle and other programmes. FY27 growth guided at 12-15% underlying; the 17.5% Q1 underlying growth is the base for the one- and three-year outlook.

qa_highlights.question: How will price increases flow through and where should margins go over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said some customer corrections for manufacturing cost inflation are still pending and expected in Q2 and Q3. FY27 target is at least 1% EBITDA margin improvement; no firm FY28-29 margin guidance beyond aspiration toward prior levels.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume growth slow after 17% in Q1 versus 12-15% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no clear reason for a slowdown currently, though quarter-by-quarter volatility remains. Guidance was corrected to 12-15%, not 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Is ROCE weak despite high utilisation, and what is the capex payback threshold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 ROCE was 10.7%, with a target of about 15% through process tweaks and exiting low-value business. Typical capex payback is 3-4 years. Loss-making JLR-linked investments are expected to turn around in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What changed versus past order book claims that did not materialise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said past EV bets had long validation periods and JLR volumes fell or SOPs slipped. Current order book focuses on ICE, hybrid and structural parts with shorter validation, and growth now comes from traditional products.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the development spend went into capacity and what is the non-auto strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Development spend went into larger, heavier parts (28-30 kg vs earlier 12-15 kg), requiring new machines and dedicated teams. Intangible spend about Rs 18-20 crore last year, Rs 3-5 crore per quarter. Non-auto aspiration unchanged but about 2% today; management expects meaningful change by end-FY28.
